title: How Trump's newest tariffs could impact Americans and the economy
summary: Lisa Desjardins reports on the administration's new round of tariffs on China, the EU and a dozen other partners, with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer arguing in a clip that foreign excess capacity is hurting American manufacturing. Wall Street Journal trade reporter Gavin Bade explains that the White House is rebuilding its tariffs on a sturdier legal footing, Section 301, after the Supreme Court struck down the earlier emergency-based duties, and that the China rate is roughly what Beijing expected ahead of the January truce deadline. He adds that consumers will feel the costs gradually rather than as a sudden shock, and that a market heavily concentrated in a few tech names is fragile and jittery.
focus: Shadow Gavin Bade's answer on when consumers will feel the tariffs, where he describes costs seeping into prices as company inventories run down, then his explanation of why the switch to Section 301 gives the tariffs firmer legal ground.
